symbols.name: Ptilde

assumptions.condition: For \(t=1,2\), \(\Pr(Y_t=y\mid X_t=x,u)=p_x(y,u)\) for every \(x,y\in B\) and \(u>0\).

standard.name: Binary panel logit response with scalar fixed heterogeneity

assumptions.condition: \(\mu\) is a probability measure on \(\mathbb R_{++}\).
\(g_{xy}(z,u)\ge0\) and \(\sum_{z\in B}g_{xy}(z,u)=1\) for every \(x,y\in B\) and \(\mu\)-almost every \(u\).
The observed vectors \((X_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), are independent and identically distributed with cell law \(P\).

standard.name: Relative-interior condition for a convex value function

definitions.name: Quartic generalized-moment construction
definitions.construction: For every \(s\in S\), set \(d\rho_s=D_c^{-1}d\nu_s\) and \(m_{s,k}=\int u^k d\rho_s\) for \(k=0,\ldots,4\).

definitions.name: Weak finite Stieltjes lift
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)=\{(m,a,b)\in\mathbb R^{56}: H_s\succeq0,\ K_s\succeq0\ \forall s\in S;\ P(x,y,z,w)=\sum_{r:r_y=z}L_{m_{(x,r)}}(A_{xz,yw})\ \forall(x,y,z,w)\in B^4;\ \Delta=\sum_{s\in S}L_{m_s}(N_c)\}\).

definitions.name: Strict finite Stieltjes lift
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_c^{+}(P,\Delta)=\{(m,a,b,t)\in\mathbb R^{64}:(m,a,b)\in\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta),\ R_s\succeq0\ \forall s\in S\}\).

definitions.name: Endpoint inclusion tests
definitions.construction: For \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), test lower inclusion by \(\mathcal F_c^v(P,L_c^v(P))\neq\varnothing\) and upper inclusion by \(\mathcal F_c^v(P,U_c^v(P))\neq\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Rank-stratified boundary handle
definitions.construction: Use \(Bhandle\) to derive the tangent feasible correspondence and directional endpoint maps on each Hankel-rank stratum, with explicit matching across the rank-fourteen observable map at \(c=1\) and the rank-sixteen map at \(c\ne1\).

statements.statement:
A law and APE generated by some \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\) are equivalent to eight nonnegative measures \((
u_s)_{s\in S}\) with \(\sum_s
u_s\) a probability measure and \[P(x,y,z,w)=\sum_{r:r_y=z}\int p_x(y,u)p_z(w,u)d
u_{(x,r)}(u),\qquad \Delta=\sum_{s\in S}\int rac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}d
u_s(u).\] Conversely, every such family reconstructs one legal base law by \(\mu=\sum_s
u_s\), initial probabilities by Radon--Nikodym derivatives of \(\sum_r
u_{(x,r)}\) with respect to \(\mu\), and feedback probabilities by the corresponding response-coordinate marginals.
statements.justification: This equivalence is the legal-kernel reconstruction step that prevents incompatible history-specific mixing laws.
statements.gap: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham use history densities satisfying pointwise compatibility; they do not replace them by eight jointly reconstructible response measures.
statements.consumer: It turns the continuous-feedback identification problem into eight independent univariate moment problems without changing the model class.

statements.statement: For any \(m_s=(m_{s,0},\ldots,m_{s,4})\in\mathbb R^5\), there is a finite nonnegative measure \(\rho_s\) on \((0,\infty)\) with these five moments if and only if there exist \(a_s,b_s\in\mathbb R\) such that \(H_s\succeq0\) and \(K_s\succeq0\). This equivalence includes the zero vector and every singular Hankel-rank regime.
statements.justification: Open-half-line representability rules out spurious mass at zero and escape to infinity without adding tail moments as assumptions.
statements.gap: Curto--Fialkow and Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell supply closed-half-line Hankel-extension tools; the exact degree-four open-half-line augmentation and singular audit are not stated for this feedback lift.
statements.consumer: It supplies the finite certificate used in every type block of the exact sharp set.

statements.statement: Let \(m_s\ne0\) for every \(s\in S\), and suppose each \(m_s\) is representable on \((0,\infty)\). The vectors admit finite representing measures on one common positive-node set with every measure assigning strictly positive weight to every node if and only if \(\operatorname{Range}(H_s)=\operatorname{Range}(H_{\Sigma})\) for every \(s\in S\). Moreover, under \(H_s\succeq0\), these range equalities hold if and only if some \(t_s\) make all \(R_s\succeq0\).
statements.justification: Mutual absolute continuity of all type measures is exactly what strict initial assignment and strict feedback require.
statements.gap: The nearest dynamic-logit Stieltjes result checks separate moment representability and has no simultaneous common-support certificate for reconstructed feedback kernels.
statements.consumer: It makes strict almost-everywhere positivity finitely testable without imposing a numerical overlap margin.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(c>0\), every \(P\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive	ext{-}observed	ext{-}cells}\), and every \(\Delta\), the independently model-defined legal fibers obey \[ (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)
e\varnothing,\qquad (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_{+}(P)\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal F_c^{+}(P,\Delta)
e\varnothing. \] The weak certificate uses exactly fifty-six scalar lift variables, eight \(3	imes3\) PSD blocks, and eight augmented \(4	imes4\) PSD blocks; the strict certificate uses sixty-four variables and eight additional \(6	imes6\) common-Hankel-range blocks. In the forward direction, each legal \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_v(c)\) is mapped to the eight joint response measures \(d
u_{(x,r_0,r_1)}=h_xg_{x0}(r_0,\cdot)g_{x1}(r_1,\cdot)d\mu\), and then to \(dho_s=D_c^{-1}d
u_s\) and its five quartic moments. In the reverse direction, every feasible lift yields positive-half-line representing measures \((ho_s)_{s\in S}\); after setting \(d
u_s=D_c dho_s\), the construction \(\mu=\sum_{s\in S}
u_s\) and the Radon--Nikodym reconstructions in \(\mathrm{lem{:}response	ext{-}measure	ext{-}equivalence}\) produce one unconditional probability law together with legal initial and feedback kernels that generate exactly \(P\) and \(\Delta\). For \(v=+\), the common-Hankel-range blocks yield representing measures on one positive-node set with strictly positive type weights, so the reconstructed \(h_x\) and \(g_{xy}\) satisfy the strict legal class. These equivalences are a strict finite-dimensional tightening of the continuous-support program in Proposition 1 of Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham while describing the same weak and strict legal model fibers.
statements.justification: The theorem removes support-grid approximation and the latent-law quantifier from the sharp continuous-heterogeneity feedback problem.
statements.gap: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham leave the continuous program infinite-dimensional, while Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell do not reconstruct an unrestricted feedback kernel.
statements.consumer: The exact cone replaces support-grid robustness bounds in a two-wave version of the Arellano--Carrasco predetermined-children design.

statements.statement: For each fixed \(c>0\) and \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), the nonempty fiber \(\{\Delta:(\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_v(P)\}\) is an interval whose infimum and supremum equal the optimal values of the two linear semidefinite programs over \(\mathcal F_c^v(P,\Delta)\). Endpoint inclusion is equivalent to the separate feasibility tests in \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoint\text{-}attainment\text{-}test}\); neither inclusion is inferred from closed PSD constraints alone.
statements.justification: Sharp numerical bounds require correct treatment of nonattainment on open-support moment faces.
statements.gap: The grid program reports numerical endpoints but does not separate sharp infima and suprema from endpoint inclusion under continuous heterogeneity.
statements.consumer: An applied researcher can report open, closed, or half-open APE bounds rather than silently treating every solver value as attainable.

statements.statement: If the entries of \(P\), \(c\), and a queried \(\Delta\) are real algebraic, then membership in either \(\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)\) or \(\Theta_{+}(P)\), projection onto \(c\) or \(\Delta\), the algebraic endpoint values, and their inclusion flags are decided by a terminating real-closed-field quantifier-elimination procedure applied to the principal-minor form of the finite lift.
statements.justification: The finite representation yields an exact decision procedure even on singular and weakly infeasible faces.
statements.gap: Existing implementations use slope grids and numerical convex solvers; no exact algebraic membership and endpoint-inclusion result is stated for the feedback model.
statements.consumer: It provides a correctness benchmark for certified solvers and eliminates arbitrary support and slope grids for algebraically encoded inputs.

statements.statement: Corollary (whole-set inversion). Under independent sampling, the inversion \(\widehat\Theta_v^{1-\eta}=\bigcup_{P'\in\Gamma_n(1-\eta)}\Theta_v(P')\) satisfies \(\Pr_P\{\Theta_v(P)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_v^{1-\eta}\}\ge1-\eta\) for \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\). The probability statement covers the entire joint sharp slope--APE set simultaneously.
statements.justification: This corollary records the direct Bonferroni consequence of simultaneous multinomial cell-law coverage and definitional set inversion.
statements.gap: Relative to Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer and the constrained inversion in Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell, this is only a model-specific exact finite-sample inversion corollary, not an independent inference theorem.
statements.consumer: The PSID robustness analysis can attach conservative simultaneous coverage to every slope and APE compatible with the population law.

statements.statement: Fix \(c>0\) and \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\). Under \(P\in\operatorname{ri}(C_c^v)\), the projected empirical law \(\widetilde P_n\) is eventually attainable almost surely and \(L_c^v(\widetilde P_n)\to L_c^v(P)\) and \(U_c^v(\widetilde P_n)\to U_c^v(P)\) almost surely.
statements.justification: This is the strongest pointwise plug-in consistency warranted by convex value-function continuity without boundary regularity.
statements.gap: The nearest Stieltjes-set estimator uses broader regularity conditions for a different conditional model; it does not verify continuity for the reconstructed feedback cone.
statements.consumer: It justifies fixed-slope endpoint estimation for attainable interior empirical designs while displaying the exact boundary excluded from the claim.

statements.statement: At \(c=1\), every legal model has \(\Delta=0\), so each nonempty fixed-slope APE fiber reduces to \(\{0\}\). The observed-law coefficient map has rank fourteen at \(c=1\) and rank sixteen for \(c\ne1\); thus the affine-hull correction used by \(\widetilde P_n\) must change at the zero-slope special case.
statements.justification: The reduction checks the known no-slope APE and exposes the rank loss that prevents an unjustified joint consistency claim.
statements.gap: Neither closest comparator supplies the rank-stratified feedback-law reduction at \(c=1\).
statements.consumer: It supplies a diagnostic for implementations and the base stratum for the open boundary-inference problem.

statements.statement: Using the rank-stratified handle in \(\mathrm{def{:}boundary\text{-}handle}\), can one construct a joint-set estimator and confidence procedure that is Hausdorff consistent and uniformly covers \(\Theta_v(P^{(n)})\) along all positive-cell attainable sequences \((P^{(n)},c_n)\to(P,1)\), including relative-boundary limits at which Hankel ranks or endpoint attainment change? If full uniformity is impossible, characterize the maximal collection of adjacent rank strata on which it holds and exhibit a least-favorable sequence outside that collection.
statements.justification: The unresolved content is the behavior of exact sharp endpoints when both the observable map and moment faces change rank.
statements.gap: Generic set inference, the model-specific regular SDP procedure, and tractable outer bounds do not settle uniform exact-set inference through this rank change.
statements.consumer: A confidence region for a slope near zero or a positive but boundary-attainable PSID law requires precisely this result.

sampling_model.design: Observational short panel with a fixed two-period design and exact cell-law inversion.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent units drawn from the population law \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: The binary predetermined covariate \(X_t\) is not randomized; its initial assignment and feedback may depend arbitrarily on \(u\).
sampling_model.overlap: The population sixteen-cell law is positive; the weak model allows zero latent assignment or feedback probabilities, while the strict model requires almost-everywhere positivity without a numerical lower bound.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cell law is estimated by multinomial frequencies; the finite-sample inversion uses simultaneous Clopper--Pearson intervals, and fixed-slope point estimation projects frequencies onto the attainable affine hull.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 1 verifies membership by feasibility of a finite- or infinite-dimensional linear program.
Theorem 3.1 characterizes the identified set by conditional moment equalities with generalized moments in a truncated Stieltjes cone.
Theorem 1 characterizes all feedback and heterogeneity robust moment conditions for the common parameter.
The main theorem replaces a latent distribution by a finite-dimensional identification-equivalent distribution for discrete covariates.
The paper constructs root-\(n\) outer bounds and asymptotically valid confidence intervals for average-effect identified sets.

tldr: In a two-period binary logit panel with one predetermined binary covariate, continuous unrestricted heterogeneity, and arbitrarily heterogeneous feedback, the model-generated joint slope--APE fibers are characterized exactly by eight joint response-type measures and a finite quartic Stieltjes lift. The weak model uses fifty-six scalar variables with eight \(3\times3\) and eight augmented \(4\times4\) PSD blocks; strict almost-everywhere assignment and feedback positivity adds eight variables and eight \(6\times6\) common-range blocks. The same representation yields sharp fixed-slope endpoint programs with separate attainment tests, terminating algebraic membership and projection, and pointwise endpoint consistency on relative-interior attainable laws; direct Bonferroni inversion gives conservative exact multinomial whole-set coverage as a corollary. Uniform exact-set inference at rank-changing boundary laws and through \(c=1\) remains the explicit open problem.

project_justification.gap: The sharp unrestricted-feedback program of Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham is infinite-dimensional for continuous heterogeneity and is evaluated on support grids. The finite Stieltjes representation of Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell does not include a separately unknown heterogeneity-dependent feedback kernel or its reconstruction from one unconditional mixing law.
project_justification.niche: At two periods, joint feedback response types preserve legal sequential kernels, while the binary-logit likelihood shares a quartic denominator whose first five generalized moments are bounded for every heterogeneity law. This creates an exact low-order open-half-line moment problem with a finite simultaneous-support certificate.
project_justification.fill: The project first defines the weak and strict sharp fibers by laws generated from the published legal feedback classes, then proves their equivalence to forward-constructed joint response measures and reverse-reconstructed legal kernels, exact open-half-line and common-range PSD certificates, and sharp endpoint and attainment formulas; exact multinomial whole-set coverage is recorded only as the direct set-inversion corollary.

related_work: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023), Proposition 1, define the sharp unrestricted-feedback identified set and motivate the response-density formulation; Theorem 4 supplies a strict finite-dimensional tightening of their continuous-support computation for \(T=2\). Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026), Theorems 3.1--3.2, supply the rational-mixture and truncated-Stieltjes method adapted here, but their known conditional likelihood does not contain the unknown feedback kernel. Curto and Fialkow (1991) and Bayer and Teichmann (2002) supply the moment-extension and finite-atomic tools used to treat singular open-half-line faces. Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2026) characterize feedback-robust moment equalities and explain why signed moment restrictions can exceed the positive sharp model. Gu, Russell, and Stringham (2026) give a complementary finite latent-cell method for discrete-outcome index models; their deterministic-cell enumeration does not remove the continuous logit mixing integral considered here. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) and Pakel and Weidner (2026) inform the unresolved rank-changing inference question. Arellano and Carrasco (2003) provide the predetermined-children labor-participation design that consumes exact feedback-robust bounds.
technical_internal_limitation: The strict common-support argument is existential and does not yet give an efficient atom-extraction routine. Real quantifier elimination establishes termination but not polynomial complexity or numerical stability. Positive observed cells do not imply strict latent assignment or feedback, a closed lifted cone need not have a closed linear image, and endpoint solver values therefore require the stated inclusion tests.
honest_scope: The model-generated weak and strict fibers are the primitive identified objects. Their exact finite-certificate equivalences, legal-kernel converses, fixed-slope endpoints, algebraic decision, and relative-interior pointwise consistency are theorem-level targets. Finite-sample whole-set coverage is a direct Bonferroni set-inversion corollary and carries no independent inference kernel. Boundary-uniform inference, joint consistency through \(c=1\), efficient certified numerical extraction, arbitrary \(T\), Markov feedback restrictions, and multinomial outcomes remain open. No numerical overlap margin, tail moment, latent density, or support grid is imposed.

seed_details.anchor_location: Proposition 1, its converse proof, Sections 5.1--5.3, the Introduction, and the Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Replace the continuous-support infinite-dimensional sharp feedback program by an exact finite lift that preserves one unconditional heterogeneity law, including singular faces and zero feedback probabilities.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace separate history densities by eight joint \((X_1,r_0,r_1)\) response-type measures before clearing the common quartic logit denominator.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for unrestricted feedback combined with Stieltjes moments, common-support Hankel ranges, and dynamic logit returned the two component papers but no joint reconstruction theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell because their general likelihood factorization already yields a finite Stieltjes program.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their Assumption 2.1 requires a known conditional likelihood given the observed conditioning variables; the unknown heterogeneity-dependent feedback kernel is not a known coefficient function, and their theorem does not reconstruct it from compatible response measures.

seed_details.anchor_location: Section 6.2 on Markovian feedback, especially the nonlinear response-density restrictions, together with the Introduction and Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Give a sharp semialgebraic characterization of the joint covariate-slope and APE set under first-order Markov feedback, including zero transition cells.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain the cross-history equality of the Markov feedback kernel as polynomial compatibility restrictions rather than conditioning it away.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found Shin's conditional-likelihood results and the Stieltjes moment machinery, but no sharp Markov-feedback slope--APE set.
seed_details.red_team: Shin already settles Markov feedback by sufficient statistics.
seed_details.rebuttal: Shin identifies selected coefficients under two specific Markov kernels and explicitly shows the general covariate slope is not recovered by conditional likelihood; that is not a sharp set characterization.

seed_details.anchor_location: Proposition 1 for arbitrary fixed \(T\), Section 5.2 on continuous-support grids, and the Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Construct an exact fixed-\(T\) finite lift with an explicit dimension bound and a legal sequential-kernel reconstruction algorithm.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Find the minimal moment collection shared by exponentially many response histories before proving their local atomic representations glue to one unconditional law.
seed_details.destination_search: Dano gives recursive rational restrictions and Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell give general-\(T\) Stieltjes growth without a separately reconstructed feedback tree; no synthesis was found.
seed_details.red_team: This is only the two-period construction with larger matrices.
seed_details.rebuttal: For \(T>2\), local history measures must satisfy sequential marginal compatibility and share a common base law; neither property follows from enlarging a Hankel block.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorems 4.1 and 4.2, the constrained-minimum-distance construction, the Introduction, and the Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Derive uniform endpoint inference across changing Hankel ranks, relative-boundary attainable laws, and local sequences \(c_n\to1\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace regular separation of the SDP criterion by a rank-stratified directional expansion of the feasible correspondence.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found generic criterion-set inference and stable outer bounds, but no limit law for this rank-changing feedback cone.
seed_details.red_team: Generic set-inference theory already gives uniform coverage.
seed_details.rebuttal: The observable map loses rank at \(c=1\), endpoint attainment can switch, and perturbations cross singular PSD faces, so the available regularity conditions do not mechanically verify.
seed_details.decision: drop after deepening because the primitive local-sequence regularity class is not yet defensible

seed_details.anchor_location: Section 5.2, Lemmas 7--8, the partial-fraction appendix, the Introduction, and the Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize sharp multinomial slope and average-effect sets under continuous heterogeneity and unrestricted feedback by a multivariate moment or sums-of-squares lift.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the scalar Stieltjes sequence by a multivariate positive-orthant moment problem and impose compatibility among category-specific feedback measures.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found multinomial fixed-effects moment restrictions and generic latent-space enumeration, but no exact unrestricted-feedback multivariate lift.
seed_details.red_team: Generic latent-space enumeration already makes every discrete-outcome model finite.
seed_details.rebuttal: Enumeration discretizes deterministic index regions; it does not exactly integrate continuously varying multinomial logit probabilities through an unrestricted feedback kernel.
seed_details.decision: drop because a bounded-order exact multivariate certificate is not presently supported

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 3.2, Algorithm 1, the Introduction, and the Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Give terminating exact membership, endpoint-inclusion, and global slope-projection algorithms for algebraic cell laws.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace floating-point SDP gridding by principal-minor formulas and real-closed-field quantifier elimination.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper was found that supplies exact algebraic projection for the unrestricted-feedback identified set.
seed_details.red_team: Tarski--Seidenberg makes termination immediate once any semialgebraic lift is written.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection holds as a standalone contribution; the result is retained only as a corollary of the identification theorem.

seed_details.anchor_location: The Introduction, Section 4 empirical specification, and the Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Replace grid sensitivity in the predetermined-children labor-participation design by an exact joint slope--APE region and whole-set confidence region.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Map the empirical two-wave cell law into the response-measure cone before propagating multinomial sampling uncertainty.
seed_details.destination_search: The empirical papers impose conditional-mean or parametric feedback restrictions; no continuous-heterogeneity exact robustness region was found.
seed_details.red_team: This is an application with no theorem beyond the proposed cone.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for a first-version mathematical core; the PSID exercise is a consumer rather than the kernel.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 3.2 and its proof via Hankel extensions, together with the Introduction and Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize when several quartic Stieltjes vectors admit mutually equivalent finite representing measures by equality of Hankel ranges.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Move from separate representability to simultaneous positive weights on a common finite positive-node support.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for finite common-support quartic Stieltjes criteria did not locate an econometric reconstruction result.
seed_details.red_team: This is a small truncated-moment lemma without an econometric estimand.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds in isolation; the criterion is valuable only as the strict-feedback half of the response-cone theorem.

seed_details.anchor_location: Assumption 2, its discussion of non-interior feedback, the Introduction, and the Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Derive a critical lower feedback-probability margin at which a sign conclusion for the APE changes.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Impose a common quantitative Radon--Nikodym lower bound and optimize the margin jointly with the endpoint.
seed_details.destination_search: No critical-margin analysis was found for feedback-logit bounds.
seed_details.red_team: The margin is an arbitrary stronger assumption chosen to tighten the answer.
seed_details.rebuttal: Without an externally calibrated margin the objection holds, so this angle is rejected rather than promoted.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 3.2, Theorem 4.1, the Introduction, and the Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the joint set-valued limit as the slope odds \(c\) crosses one and the observable coefficient map loses rank.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Blow up the rank-deficient coefficient map at \(c=1\) and match its tangent image to the adjacent Hankel faces.
seed_details.destination_search: No dynamic-logit paper located in the search gives a joint-in-slope set limit at this rank change.
seed_details.red_team: This is a technical continuity appendix with no new identified object.
seed_details.rebuttal: The rank-stratified limit would be new, but its consumer depends on the finite-cone theorem; it is therefore retained as the core open-ended question rather than a separate seed.
seed_details.decision: fold into selected seed as open content

threads: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023), Proposition 1 and its converse, give the sharp unrestricted-feedback program; Section 5.2 says continuous heterogeneity makes it infinite-dimensional and uses support grids.

Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026), Theorems 3.1--3.2, factor a known rational conditional likelihood through generalized moments and certify positive-half-line representability by Hankel PSD extensions.

Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2026), Theorem 1 and Supplemental Appendix E, characterize feedback-robust moment equalities; the appendix shows that dropping positivity produces a closed outer region, not the full sharp latent-law set.

Gu, Russell, and Stringham (2026), Theorems 1--2 and the profiling algorithm, replace latent distributions by finitely many deterministic response regions for linear-index discrete-outcome models; this does not integrate continuously varying logit probabilities under unknown feedback.
Curto and Fialkow (1991), Theorem 5.1 and Lemma 2.3, supply the truncated Stieltjes extension result adapted to the open half-line certificate.
literature_map.occupancy_check: No located paper joins joint feedback-response measures, open-half-line quartic Stieltjes representability, and simultaneous reconstruction of one unconditional heterogeneity law.

threads: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023), Section 6.2, explicitly leaves the nonlinear Markov-feedback sharp-set restrictions open.
Shin (2025), Propositions 1--2, uses sufficient statistics for two Markov feedback specifications and shows the general covariate coefficient can lose conditional-likelihood variation.
Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026) provide the univariate Stieltjes component after a legal Markov response representation is obtained.
Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2026) provide feedback-robust moments and efficiency theory but do not impose the nonlinear Markov kernel equalities needed for sharpness.
literature_map.occupancy_check: The exact Markov target remains unoccupied, but denominator-zero regimes make the reconstruction materially less feasible than the selected unrestricted-feedback seed.

threads: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023), Proposition 1, covers every fixed \(T\) but retains a continuous-index nuisance program.
Dano (2025), the transition-function lemmas and partial-fraction appendix, show how rational logit algebra scales with lags and multinomial choices under strict exogeneity.
Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026) show finite generalized-moment growth in several dynamic logit models without an unknown feedback tree.
Gu, Russell, and Stringham (2026) give finite latent-cell enumeration for discrete outcomes but not a common-kernel continuous-logit moment lift.
literature_map.occupancy_check: No closer paper subsumes the kernel, but the sequential compatibility proof is not yet reduced to a defensible finite certificate.

literature_checklist.author: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham

literature_checklist.author: Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 3.1--3.2 give generalized-moment identification and Hankel extension conditions for known rational likelihoods.

literature_checklist.author: Curto and Fialkow
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 5.1 and Lemma 2.3 characterize truncated Stieltjes sequences through recursive Hankel extensions.

literature_checklist.author: Bayer and Teichmann

literature_checklist.author: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 1 characterizes feedback-robust moments, while Supplemental Appendix E distinguishes their signed outer region from the positive sharp set.

literature_checklist.author: Gu, Russell, and Stringham
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 1--2 use finite latent-space cells and linear programs for discrete-outcome counterfactual bounds.

literature_checklist.author: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper derives consistency and confidence regions for criterion-defined identified sets.

novelty_justification: {"anti_pattern_check":"The kernel uses the non-LP Stieltjes-cone motif because the nuisance is a rational mixture, not because partial identification defaults to linear programming. The PSD blocks, joint response measures, legal reverse kernel, endpoint-attainment flags, and common-range certificate are named evaluable objects. The open question has a rank-stratified tangent-cone handle.","closest_results":["Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023), Proposition 1, is sharp for unrestricted feedback but is infinite-dimensional under continuous heterogeneity and is computed by support grids.","Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026), Theorems 3.1--3.2, give finite Stieltjes restrictions for a known rational conditional likelihood but do not reconstruct an unknown heterogeneity-dependent feedback kernel."],"precise_gap":"The missing theorem is an if-and-only-if finite representation that both preserves one unconditional heterogeneity measure across feedback histories and remains exact on singular open-half-line moment faces.","selected_seed":"seed:exact-t2-response-stieltjes-cone","strict_delta":"The weak and strict slope--APE fibers are defined directly by the same legal model classes used by Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham. The exact-cone theorem independently proves that the finite response-type certificates are equivalent to those fibers, including the reverse construction of one unconditional heterogeneity law and legal feedback kernels, rather than defining the target by the lift."}
